title: National Government
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 5 Social Studies; not yet checked by a CBC Social Studies teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Three arms as three boxes: the Legislature makes laws, the Executive carries them out, the Judiciary interprets them and settles disputes. Name offices, never office holders or parties.

skills.key_step: The child says what each arm does: the Legislature makes laws, the Executive carries them out, the Judiciary interprets them and settles disputes.

floor.prerequisite: Knows the county executive and county assembly.
floor.question: Which part of the county government makes county laws?

representations: a role play: making, carrying out and judging a rule
steps: Place it in the right arm.
contexts: Parliament passing a law on plastic bags
a court hearing a case about it

board.do: Draw three boxes: Legislature, Executive, Judiciary.
Write a duty in each box.

misconceptions.ask: Which arm of government makes laws?
misconceptions.repair: Use one verb per arm: runs, makes, explains.
Show that each arm checks the others.

misconceptions.ask: How many arms does the National Government have?
misconceptions.repair: Draw the three boxes and put a judge's gavel in the third.

misconceptions.ask: Who decides whether a person accused of stealing is guilty?
misconceptions.repair: Act it: the police arrest, the magistrate hears both sides and decides.

skills.key_step: The child places people and bodies in the right arm and keeps county offices out of the national arms.

floor.question: Which arm carries out the laws?

representations: a county box at the side
steps: Match the duty to the arm.
If it is a county office, place it in the county box.
contexts: a judge in the High Court
a Cabinet Secretary opening a project

board.say: Is the Governor in the National Government?

board.do: Place the others in their arms.

misconceptions.ask: To which arm do judges belong?
misconceptions.repair: Place each title in one of three boxes by its job.

misconceptions.ask: Which of these is part of the National Government's Executive?
misconceptions.repair: Draw two levels: county and national.

misconceptions.ask: In which arm is the Senate?
misconceptions.repair: Place the Senate card next to the National Assembly card in the Legislature box.

misconceptions.ask: Are Cabinet Secretaries members of Parliament?
misconceptions.repair: Sort each office into the three boxes again with the rule: who carries out the law?

checks.question: In which arm is a magistrate?
Is a Member of the County Assembly part of the National Legislature?
